newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH SHORT-TERM RATES JUMP AFTER CENBANK MOVES.
newsitem.headline: CZECH SHORT-TERM RATES JUMP AFTER CENBANK MOVES.

text.p: The Czech interbank overnight offered rate jumped up to 100 percent on Tuesday after the central bank limited bank access to Lombard loans further squeezing liquidity in an already short market, dealers said.

David Netusil of Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka said branches of foreign banks with small amounts of capital in the Czech Republic were hit hardest as the Czech National Bank (CNB) limited access to the last resort rate to an amount equal to an unspecified portion of an individual bank's capital.
The average overnight offered rate on Monday was 34.93 percent, according to CNB calculations.

"The central bank drained money through repo tenders, and only after the deadline of the repo, banks, mainly branches of foreign banks, calculated how much they were missing, and begun to drain the overnight which went over 80 percent," he said.
He added that banks wanted to turn to the Lombard, but the central bank restricted access.
"They failed to get into the Lombard, so the overnight is very, very short, maybe some banks will fail to fulfil the minimum reserve requirements. They are now paying even 100 percent," he said.
The central bank held three repo tenders -- overnight, tomorrow/next and spot next -- on Tuesday morning with average yields reaching 44.58, 44.45 and 44.14 percent respectively.

Netusil said tommorrow/next day rates were 55 to 75 percent, while the one week bid rate jumped to 50 percent from Monday's 25.83 percent. He added that long-term funds jumped about four points from Monday.
The CNB raised the Lombard rate to 50 percent on Friday from 14 percent to prevent short selling of the local currency, and also raised the repo rate to 45 percent from 12.9 percent.
